title: ViewportTexture breaks on reload if set directly on mesh material
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: All 4.X releases. 3.6.2 also shows similar symptoms, but alas it's very different from the current release so I'm not fully sure if I tested it in the same way (correctly).

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated Intel(R) Arc(TM) B580 Graphics (Intel Corporation; 32.0.101.8509) - AMD Ryzen 9 7900 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 63.61 GiB memory

### Issue description

Assigning a ViewportTexture to a mesh material as Albedo Texture should work after reloading the project. Unfortunately it breaks until I manually clear and reassing it and then breaks again as soon as the scene is (re)loaded.

I found #115402 which seems to be somewhat related, although it was 2D and texture only without a material and mesh.

I also found [this comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs-user-notes/discussions/608#discussioncomment-15547580) and it turns out that the problem is fixed if the mesh itself is also local to the scene (not just the material and the ViewportTexture). The editor gives no warning about the mesh not being local, only when the material is not local.

Additionally if reproduction steps 5 and 6 are done on the Surface Material Override instead of directly on the mesh material, then everything is fine even after a reload.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new scene, add a MeshInstance3D
2. (Optional for better editing) Add a SubViewportContainer
3. Add a SubViewport and create a child Label to this SubViewport (add some text for better visibility)
4. On the MeshInstance3D create a new QuadMesh (or any other mesh really)
5. Add a new material on the mesh and set it as Local to Scene in the Resource category
6. Go to the material Albedo category and create a new ViewportTexture, then assign the SubViewport to it (the mesh should now display the viewport)
7. Reload the scene and watch the texture break (even better if you close the editor and open the project again, because then you get a pink placeholder)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[viewport-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25419264/viewport-test.zip)
